name: Interactive Brokers
summary: IBKR supplies Linux builds of TWS and IB Gateway. Alpharch’s development desk now includes a read-only futures bridge, contract selection and charts. Offline checks pass; a real gateway, account and CME data connection have not yet been acceptance-tested.
needs: An IBKR account and its required market-data subscriptions.
The Linux TWS or IB Gateway application, signed in locally.
The official TWS API Python client installed in the same runtime as Alpharch. This is optional for public crypto tools.
The development desk with the IBKR bridge. This guide is not a claim that the public installer includes a supported broker connection.
steps: Install the official Linux application
Download TWS or IB Gateway from IBKR. Gateway uses fewer desktop resources; TWS also lets you inspect the same data in its own interface.
Prepare the local API connection
In the application’s API settings, enable socket clients, retain read-only access for charting, and note the socket port. Keep access on this computer.
Install the optional official API client

Use the TWS API download and IBKR’s Python installation instructions linked below. Follow the downloaded version’s dependency requirements. The development desk shows Setup required when the client is missing.
Connect the development desk

Open Connect, choose Interactive Brokers, and enter the local API port and a unique nonzero client ID. Sign-in stays in TWS or IB Gateway; Alpharch does not ask for your broker password. A port number alone does not verify paper or live account mode.
Choose the exact futures contract

Search the futures root and exchange, then select the actual expiry and contract returned by IBKR. Alpharch uses the returned contract ID and price increments; it does not automatically pick the first expiry.
Confirm your market data

Check the exact contract and exchange in IBKR. Quotes, tick-by-tick subscriptions and market depth have different permissions and limits. Keep delayed, frozen or unknown status visible. This development connection requires account acceptance testing before it can be called supported.
trouble: Gateway opens but no chart data
Check that you are signed in, the API is enabled and the socket port matches. A successful socket connection alone does not establish a market-data entitlement.
Cumulative delta or a bid/ask footprint is unavailable

IBKR’s tick-by-tick Last callback does not provide aggressor side. Alpharch leaves it unknown; it does not invent buy/sell volume from watchlist quotes. Trade volume can still be shown without directional classification.
A ladder is missing detail
Check depth permissions and subscription limits. The bridge receives positional Level-2 updates, not individual-order MBO data.
What has actually been tested?

Twenty bridge checks pass against official SDK 10.50.1 in an isolated runtime, including decoded protocol callbacks with networking replaced. Integration checks cover exact contracts, market-rule ticks, unknown aggressor, recording/replay and delayed-depth suppression. No real gateway session, account entitlement, live CME latency or execution test has been performed. The bridge has no order methods.

name: Rithmic
summary: Rithmic is a data and routing provider used by multiple futures brokers. Its WebSocket/protobuf protocol is a route for a Linux integration; R | Trader Pro itself is a Windows application.
needs: Broker-issued Rithmic credentials, system name and market-data permissions.
Alpharch developer-kit access, implementation and successful conformance before production use.
steps: Find your feed credentials
Use the Rithmic login issued for your trading account. Your broker’s customer-portal password may be different.
Confirm the system and subscriptions
Ask the broker which Rithmic system your account uses, whether third-party access is enabled, and what depth is included.
Check Alpharch availability
The adapter is not released. Production requires Rithmic conformance; personal credentials alone cannot enable an unapproved application.
trouble: Login works elsewhere but not in another platform
Verify the exact system, application permission and simultaneous-session allowance with the broker.
Expecting MBO detail
Confirm that the account and integration deliver individual-order data. Level-2 availability by itself is not proof of MBO coverage.

name: CQG
summary: CQG can connect a Linux application through its Web API. Production access requires application identifiers and conformance; browser authorization also requires CQG app registration.
needs: A CQG account enabled by the broker for the intended application and exchanges.
Alpharch registration, adapter implementation and production conformance.
steps: Identify the CQG account
Use the CQG credentials supplied for your trading platform, not an unrelated broker-portal login.
Check account access
Confirm the exchange subscriptions and third-party platform permissions with your broker.
Use the supported authorization route when released
CQG documents user logon and registered OAuth with PKCE. Alpharch has not released either route; this website does not collect credentials.
trouble: Application or private-label error
The software’s CQG registration must match the account’s permissions. This is not fixed by repeatedly changing your password.
Quotes without depth
Ask for the data entitlement needed for the exact contract and view. Top-of-book access does not supply a full ladder.

name: Tradovate

steps: Confirm API eligibility
Check the current API-access requirements in Tradovate’s official documentation and your account settings. A platform login is not proof of API access.
Identify the environment
Keep live and simulation accounts distinct. Market-data permission is separate from the ability to sign in.
Authorize when supported
A released third-party connection should direct you through the supported authorization flow. Alpharch’s Tradovate adapter is not available yet.
trouble: Demo or prop account will not authorize
Ask the account provider whether third-party API use is allowed for that specific account.
Account appears but quotes do not
Check API and exchange-data permissions, then the exact contract symbol and environment.

name: Kraken
route: Public USD spot / separate account API
summary: Kraken BTC, ETH and SOL USD spot feeds passed live checks in Alpharch’s development desk on September 5, 2026. Kraken’s futures API is separate and is not implemented in this desk.
needs: The development chart desk with Kraken support. The public installer is a separate release.
Access to Kraken’s public market-data service from your location. No account login is needed for these charts.
steps: Open Connections in the development desk
Choose Kraken, then BTC, ETH or SOL. New Chart and Markets also offer the Kraken source.
Choose your chart
The adapter supplies actual trades, a price-level book and historical candles. Check that the chart is labeled Kraken and USD spot.
Check the received data

The live check confirmed 100 book levels per side and 720 completed one-minute historical candles for each tested market. Captured order-flow history begins at connection; candles do not supply historical aggressor classification.
Keep account access separate
The optional Kraken account adapter is read-only development code tested for protocol/error handling. It has not been accepted with a real account and is not a released broker connection.
trouble: Kraken is missing from New Chart
Your installed version may predate the development desk. This guide does not mean that the public installer has already shipped it.
Expecting Kraken futures or derivatives
This adapter covers USD spot. It does not connect Kraken Futures or transfer a derivatives subscription.
The book becomes unavailable
A failed book-integrity check or stale connection must recover before the chart is treated as current. Do not substitute another venue’s book.
sources: Kraken public and private WebSocket services
